A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCU research despite the changed title. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification unlearning experiments, baseline comparisons, and ablations in Sections 3–4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds pathway, masking, robustness, checkpoint-selection, and configuration comparisons in Section 4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The default Bezier pathway, loss, masking procedure, and pseudocode remain substantially unchanged. v2 adds a Polychain variant with one to three control points. Section 3.4 also revises the stated class-wise calibration target to zero, replacing v1's unqualified validation-accuracy reference; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, ImageNet-100, and Tiny-ImageNet under random-data and class-wise forgetting. The added CIFAR-10/VGG configuration and 1% forgetting fraction change settings, not dataset or task coverage. Appendix E's medical and harmful-information examples are hypothetical.

E2.justification: v2 adds SFRon to the existing benchmark and pre-unlearning-model comparisons while retaining all original baselines. It also introduces comparisons against Polychain pathways, linear interpolation, and SalUn/SFRon masks within MCU, substantially broadening the comparison methods beyond the original benchmark set.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include CIFAR-10 with VGG-16-BN, 1% random forgetting, alternative pathway and masking configurations, and deliberately degraded GA endpoints. The checkpoint-selection control applies MCU's selection criteria to existing RL training trajectories. These extend the evaluation protocol; most original splits and training settings remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial analyses of pathway geometry, alternative masks, adaptive-beta sensitivity to k and kr, severely degraded endpoints, and whether checkpoint selection explains MCU's advantage. The earlier fixed-beta ablations, under/over-forgetting cases, and retaining-data scarcity analyses are retained, sometimes relocated or redisplayed.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations from five independent trials. v2 extends this reporting style to additional results without introducing a new empirical uncertainty procedure, seed disclosure, or significance test. Its new probability theorem is not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries in all six original tables are unchanged, including relocated content. v2 adds substantial new results for SFRon, Polychain, CIFAR-10/VGG, 1% forgetting, masks, and diagnostic controls. For example, new Table 10 reports average gaps of 0.30 for MCU-beta and 1.38 for SalUn. The reported cross-method gap reduction changes from 49.71% to 48.99% with the expanded comparator set.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 3.1 and Appendix B's formal assumptions and proof bounding the number of independent models needed under uniformly distributed optimal stopping epochs, followed by a proposed generalization. The original weight-entanglement derivation remains in Appendix A. Polychain and linear-interpolation formulations are also added.

C1.justification: The core MCU contribution remains, but v2 strengthens the motivation from flexibility among solutions to a claimed fundamental insufficiency of a single unlearning model. It presents the continuous pathway as resolving this difficulty and explicitly claims the first nonlinear investigation of unlearning. These extend the scientific claims beyond v1's practical trade-off argument.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking linear interpolation's failure to loss barriers, Bezier performance to smooth optimization, and MCU's advantage to continuous exploration rather than checkpoint selection. It discusses endpoint-quality dependence and the stopping-epoch assumptions, and adds hypothetical applications involving changing privacy or safety requirements. These are substantive interpretations beyond the retained discussion.

D1.justification: v2 announces a code-repository link and specifies the confidence-based SVC membership attack, balanced attack-training data, and nonmembership metric. It adds SFRon and CIFAR-10/VGG training settings and clarifies tensor-level masking. Conversely, v1's three-stage runtime breakdown is removed. The linked repository's contents or accessibility cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes MCU from Cheng and Amiri's concurrent use of mode connectivity for evaluation, and uses Georgiev et al. to motivate the new single-model insufficiency argument. Additional work supports the discussions of linear connectivity, robustness, and membership attacks. These changes substantively expand research positioning beyond citation-format updates.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, the introduction gains contribution bullets, alignment terminology becomes calibration terminology, and the retaining-data discussion moves to the appendix. Disclosure sections are added and appendices reorganized. Nevertheless, the main section sequence and much existing explanatory prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds multiple pathway, robustness, and checkpoint figures and comparison tables. It moves the Tiny-ImageNet block from Table 1 to Appendix Table 5 and the retaining-data summary from Figure 2 to Figure 11. The conference template changes headers and typography, and appendix prose changes from two columns to one.

improvement.justification: The new checkpoint and masking controls address important empirical questions, while the MIA specification and code link improve reproducibility documentation. However, v2 uses a theorem about independent training runs to justify a continuous MCU pathway without proving that connection. Its revised class-wise target is also zero while Equation 7 divides by that target. These new theoretical and procedural gaps materially counterbalance the stronger empirical evidence, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
